verdict.summary: Connecting your own HubSpot account through your own OAuth app is quick and needs no review, since a free developer account is enough. Public Marketplace distribution is the hard part: it needs your own app, at least three active unaffiliated production installs, a manual review, and a fully documented OAuth flow with no copy-pasted tokens.
verdict.hands_on_effort: Own-account setup: about 1-3 hours (estimate). Marketplace listing prep and submission: several days of work (estimate), plus review wait.
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 1 hour (estimate), once the developer account exists.
verdict.approval_wait: None to connect your own account. Marketplace listing: initial review within 10 business days, full cycle up to 60 days from when feedback is shared (f10).

gates.name: Developer account, own-account use
gates.unlocks: Create the app with the HubSpot CLI and connect your own HubSpot account through OAuth. Composio's managed HubSpot OAuth app is also available for development and testing.
limits: Building apps does not require a paid subscription (f4).
Legacy public apps can no longer be created in the Developer Platform UI; new apps go through the Projects-based CLI (f6, f7).
Free developer accounts include test accounts (f4).

gates.name: Test and invited users (not verified)
gates.unlocks: Install the app in developer test accounts and, if you choose, in other invited portals. The findings do not confirm the exact mechanism or caps for unlisted installs.
limits: Install caps for unlisted or unreviewed public apps were not verified (see open questions).
A converted developer portal starts with two Super Admin core seats; extra team members can get developer seats without a paid CRM seat (f26).
Token expiry and refresh behaviour were not confirmed. Apps must refresh access tokens before they expire (f22).
gates.time_to_reach: Same session as Gate 1 once the app is deployed (estimate)

gates.name: Marketplace listing (public)
gates.unlocks: List the app in the HubSpot Marketplace so any customer can install it. Optional certification is a further step that adds a higher badge tier.
limits: At least three active, unique production installs in the past 30 days, unaffiliated with your organization (f9).
Manual review by the Ecosystem Quality team; rejected if criteria are missed (f10).
Only one app can be in the listing queue at a time; others are auto-rejected (f11).
No fee to list or certify, and no revenue share on Marketplace installs (f21).

Certification adds: verified domain, security assessment, demo video, six months listed, 60 active unaffiliated installs, success rate above 95% (f17, f18, f19). Reviews take up to 10 business days and up to 60 days in total; certification lasts two years (f20).
gates.time_to_reach: Initial review within 10 business days; full cycle up to 60 days from when feedback is shared (f10). Certification is a separate, later track.

steps.title: Create a free HubSpot developer account
steps.detail: Sign up for a free HubSpot developer account. You do not need a paid subscription to build and test apps. Free accounts include test accounts, API access for testing, app management and CLI access.
gotchas: A converted developer portal starts with two Super Admin core seats (f26).

steps.title: Install the HubSpot CLI and create a project
steps.detail: Install the HubSpot CLI and run hs get-started to authenticate and create your first project. Marketplace-bound apps are built with the Projects-based tooling.
gotchas: Creating legacy public apps through the Developer Platform UI was switched off on May 26, 2026 for new accounts and June 23, 2026 for older accounts. Do not look for that option (f6).

steps.title: Create the app in the project
steps.detail: Follow the create-an-app documentation to add a public app inside your Projects project. The exact console path for public apps inside a project was not confirmed, so check the current docs page for the menu names.
gotchas: The on-screen menu names for this step were not verified. Confirm them on the docs page before you start.

steps.title: Set the OAuth redirect URI to the Composio callback
steps.detail: In the app's OAuth or auth settings, set the redirect URI to the callback URL shown in your Composio HubSpot auth config. Redirect URI rules (exact match, allowed schemes, multiple URIs) were not verified, so test the connection before you rely on it.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Composio's managed HubSpot app uses its own default redirect URI. A self-registered app needs the callback from your own Composio auth config (f1).

steps.title: Declare only the scopes your app uses
steps.detail: List the CRM scopes your agent actually calls, using the scope requirements in each API reference guide. Do not copy Composio's default scope set, which is much broader. Marketplace certification requires that every requested scope is used.
gotchas: Composio's default list includes scopes such as crm.objects.custom.read, sales-email-read and content. Remove any you do not call.
Whether specific scopes are sensitive or restricted was not confirmed (see open questions).

steps.title: Connect your own account through OAuth
steps.detail: Add a HubSpot auth config in Composio using your app's client ID and client secret, then authorize with your own HubSpot account. The authorization must go through the OAuth browser flow; do not paste codes or tokens by hand.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Copy-pasted OAuth codes or tokens are prohibited for Marketplace certification (f16).
Your app must request, manage and refresh tokens without user involvement (f16).

steps.title: Deploy and verify the app with the CLI
steps.detail: Deploy the project to your HubSpot developer account with the CLI, then install the app into a test account and run one authorized API call to confirm the token works.
gotchas: Projects 2025.1 is deprecated as of June 1, 2026. Use a current platform version (f28).

steps.title: Check the platform version is supported
steps.detail: Before you plan a listing, confirm your project uses a platform version HubSpot has not declared unsupported. An unsupported version cannot be listed on the Marketplace.
gotchas: Legacy apps on older platform versions are being deprecated over time (f28).

steps.title: Draft the listing documentation and required URLs
steps.detail: Draft the setup documentation, Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, support contact, install button URL and pricing copy. Check that pricing matches the website. Host the setup docs on a live URL. Missing or wrong required fields leave the listing in Draft mode.
gotchas: The listing may not depend on another app, and OAuth must be the only authorization method (f8).
App-card names may not use HubSpot brand words, and HubSpot's name may not be combined with the app name or logo (f13).

steps.title: Check the Classic CRM cards deadline
steps.detail: If your app uses Classic CRM cards, plan to remove or replace them. Classic CRM cards sunset on October 31, 2026, two days from the date of this guide.
gotchas: Classic CRM cards are not supported in the new listing flow (f14).

steps.title: Confirm scopes are allowed on app cards
steps.detail: Check that no app card requests a sensitive-data scope or displays sensitive information. The list of sensitive CRM properties is on HubSpot's sensitive-data page, which was only seen in search results and not read in full.
gotchas: Which scopes count as sensitive was not confirmed (see open questions).

steps.title: Reach three active unaffiliated production installs
steps.detail: Get at least three unique production installs from organizations not affiliated with yours, each with OAuth-authenticated API calls or signed webhook or extension requests in the past 30 days. Test accounts do not count toward this total.
gotchas: Activity means OAuth-authenticated API calls or signed webhook and extension requests (f9).
Whether installs made through Composio's managed app count was not verified.

steps.title: Submit the listing for review
steps.detail: Submit the listing for Ecosystem Quality review. Only one app can be in the listing queue at a time, so do not submit a second app while the first is being reviewed.
gotchas: Any other app submitted while one is in the queue is automatically rejected (f11).
Listing submissions are rejected when they miss the criteria (f10).

steps.title: Wait for listing review
steps.detail: HubSpot's initial review is due within 10 business days. The whole review-and-feedback cycle should take no more than 60 days from when feedback is shared.
gotchas: If the listing is rejected, fix the criteria it missed before resubmitting.

steps.title: Optional: prepare certification
steps.detail: For certification, prepare a verified domain, a security questionnaire on encryption, access controls and token lifecycle, a demo video, and a scan of public assets. The demo video must show a user disconnecting the app, the Uninstall App endpoint being called, and the app removed from the Connected Apps page. Certification also needs six months listed, 60 active unaffiliated installs and a success rate above 95%.
gotchas: HubSpot does not review an app without the demo video (f18).
A rejected app can reapply after six months (f20).
Verified-domain setup steps were not checked (see open questions).

scopes.scope: Composio default set (35 scopes, including crm.objects.*, crm.schemas.*, settings.users.*, e-commerce, content)
scopes.effect: Requesting every scope in the default set makes the app harder to justify. Certification requires that the app use every scope it requests (f16). Reduce to the scopes you call.
Included in Composio's default set. Whether these are sensitive was not confirmed.
App cards may not access or use sensitive-data scopes or display sensitive information (f15). Which specific scopes are classed as sensitive was not confirmed.
Included in Composio's default set. Confirm whether it is needed and whether it is classed as sensitive before requesting it.

blockers.symptom: No option to create a legacy public app in the Developer Platform UI.
blockers.cause: Creating new legacy public apps through the Developer Platform UI was switched off on May 26, 2026 (new accounts) and June 23, 2026 (older accounts).
blockers.fix: Create the app with the HubSpot CLI in a Projects-based project (hs get-started).

blockers.symptom: Marketplace listing is automatically rejected while another app is being reviewed.
blockers.cause: Only one app can be in the listing approval queue at a time.
blockers.fix: Wait until the current app is decided before submitting another.

blockers.symptom: Listing cannot be submitted or is rejected on platform version.
blockers.cause: The developer-platform version is declared unsupported, or Projects 2025.1 is deprecated as of June 1, 2026.
blockers.fix: Upgrade the project to a currently supported platform version before listing.

blockers.symptom: Listing rejected or certification blocked because the auth flow uses copied codes or tokens.
blockers.cause: Asking users to copy and paste OAuth codes or tokens is prohibited, and the app must refresh tokens without user involvement.
blockers.fix: Use the standard OAuth authorization-code flow and automatic token refresh.

blockers.symptom: Listing rejected for a sensitive-data scope on an app card.
blockers.cause: App cards may not access or use sensitive-data scopes or display sensitive information.
blockers.fix: Remove the sensitive-data scope from the app card or move that feature out of the card.

blockers.symptom: CRM cards stop working after October 31, 2026.
blockers.cause: Classic CRM cards sunset on October 31, 2026.
blockers.fix: Migrate to the supported card approach before that date.

composio.note: Use Composio's managed HubSpot OAuth app for development and testing; it is the quick path and needs no app registration. Register your own app if you need to connect your own client ID, your own redirect URI, or to list on the Marketplace. Marketplace listing requires the app's own public app ID and OAuth client ID tied to the listing (f8). Whether Composio's managed app can serve a listing was not verified, so treat that as open. The default scope set is much broader than most apps need, so reduce it before you register your own app.

The HubSpot authorize endpoint is live; an invalid client_id returned a 200 HubSpot OAuth page with no OAuth error parameters.
The HubSpot Developer Platform documentation is public and showed no login wall when probed.
